name: Chromium
short: In a meta-analysis of 25 diabetes trials, adverse events were no more common than with placebo. One case report describes kidney failure and liver dysfunction after months of excess intake.
text: In a meta-analysis of 25 randomised trials in people with diabetes, the risk of adverse events did not differ between chromium and placebo; the authors noted that long-term safety remains to be investigated. A systematic review of chromium picolinate in overweight or obese adults (9 trials, 622 participants) found that only three studies reported adverse events and concluded there was no reliable evidence to inform firm decisions about safety. A case report describes a 33-year-old woman who developed anaemia, low platelets, haemolysis, liver dysfunction and renal failure after taking chromium picolinate for 4-5 months at 6-12 times the recommended daily allowance (as described in the report); her laboratory values were normal one year later. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
